claims.statement: On 2026-09-02 the v0.3.1 image listed the 2,549-key normals-hourly/ prefix of noaa-normals-pds anonymously through all eight adapter modes, each exiting 0 and normalizing to 2,549 rows, 2,549 distinct keys and one identical key-set digest.
claims.qualification: A direct docker run observation on the maintainer's workstation, not a receipt: no attempt record, no verifier verdict, no reference manifest. The count matches the registry's recorded figure for the prefix and the eight modes agree with one another, which cannot detect a substituted key or a missing key compensated by an extra one. One prefix, one run per mode, no counters compared between modes; nothing here is comparative.

claims.statement: Swath's canonical repository is github.com/varveio/swath and it is public at v0.3.1, as it was at v0.2.0.
claims.qualification: On 2026-09-02 the repository, its releases, and its container images were all publicly readable without authentication; the GitHub API reports visibility public and licence Apache-2.0.

claims.statement: Swath is written in Java on a JDK 25 toolchain.
claims.qualification: The Gradle Java-conventions build logic pins JavaLanguageVersion 25 and neither settings file registers a toolchain resolver, so a bare host needs a local JDK 25. The 0.3.1 image runs on Temurin 25.0.4.

claims.statement: At 7b9a5e2 the repository carries an Apache-2.0 LICENSE file and a NOTICE naming Varve Systems Ltd, with THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md as the authoritative attribution record.
claims.qualification: GitHub reports spdx_id Apache-2.0, and the notices file is machine-generated from the CLI runtime graph and staleness-gated by verifyThirdPartyNotices; a second, separately gated notices file covers the swath-replay distribution.

claims.statement: The tested image self-reports swath 0.3.1 with Commit: 7b9a5e2fba04 and Runtime: 25.0.4+7-LTS.
claims.qualification: Since 0.2.1 --version prints a multi-line block naming the build, source commit, Java runtime and Varve; the probe was run directly under docker run and is recorded in the v0.3.1 delta record, with no receipt.

claims.statement: Upstream publishes tagged releases with v-prefixed git tags: eight from v0.1.0 on 2026-07-27 to v0.3.1 on 2026-09-01, six of them between the two subjects this capsule has described.
claims.qualification: Release version discipline is mechanical: verifyReleaseVersion fails unless the git tag equals v plus the gradle.properties version, now also admitting an -rc.N pre-release form. v0.3.0 and v0.3.1 were published one hour apart on 2026-09-01; the 0.3.1 notes say the CLI is unchanged from 0.3.0.

claims.statement: The published image binds itself to source: both per-arch config blobs carry org.opencontainers.image.revision equal to the pinned commit 7b9a5e2fba045c67165c76511f8c40c880406a8a.
claims.qualification: The source-to-image link is embedded in the artifact rather than recorded only in a build receipt. The jar inside the image is the release build job's own uber-jar, promoted by a BuildKit build-context override and checksum-verified before use; the image is pushed by digest, smoked, and only then tagged. The label read is a direct docker inspect observation with no receipt.

claims.statement: The tested subject is upstream's own published image, an OCI index at ghcr.io/varveio/swath@sha256:776e788200a1e70f30206897303a34e4faabd56c591e1c9562277677085c4f60, pullable anonymously with no docker login.
claims.qualification: The registry tag is 0.3.1 with no v prefix, and v0.3.1 returns manifest unknown, as at 0.2.0. The index carries linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 children plus two attestation manifests, and a cosign signature tag for the index digest is present. The pull and manifest fetch were direct observations on 2026-09-02 with no receipt.

claims.statement: The study read Swath's own source at the pinned v0.2.0 and v0.3.1 tags, a first-party source basis, and the tool is built by the same organisation that runs the study.
claims.qualification: The maintainer-disclosure consequence holds whether or not the repository is public. The stated mitigation is structural: the v0.2.0 derivation was blind to the capsule pages it replaced, every claim is anchored, an independent cross-model review re-verified the anchors, and the v0.3.1 update re-tested every claim against the frozen tree rather than carrying it forward.

claims.statement: Swath divides the keyspace into half-open byte ranges scanned by virtual-thread workers that become thieves when no work is claimable, subdividing ranges at runtime by synthesizing pivot keys.
claims.qualification: The design is established from source at cef8ec2; no run instruments the internal range set. At most one steal attempt is in flight fleet-wide, and lock order is strictly victim then gate.

claims.statement: A split child is counted into the outstanding-work total while the thief still holds the victim's lock, so the engine's termination check cannot observe a false quiescence between hand-off and count.
claims.qualification: Source-established at cef8ec2: poll reports quiescent only when the ready deque is empty and outstanding is zero, and the enqueue that increments outstanding is documented and called under the victim lock. No run instruments the worklist and no fault-injection run exercised the race, so this is a design property read from source.

claims.statement: Swath's listing is adaptive and density-aware.
claims.qualification: At v0.2.0 the density-aware characterization is established from first-party source rather than from upstream's design documentation: the seed frontier is mass-ordered by default, pivot placement is driven by a trailing density EWMA, and the default remaining-work estimator is rate-anchored. Source supports the mechanism; it does not establish that range placement is density-proportional in effect at runtime.

claims.statement: Pivot placement is a multi-phase state machine whose first placement is a density-derived far-ahead fraction, with the plain byte midpoint used as a step-back target and bisection as a late phase.
claims.qualification: The default cut is not a byte-midpoint bisection: at v0.2.0 the start phase places at clamp(0.5 + 0.25 times min(1, trailing density over average density), 0.5, 0.75) on a bounded range, and the plain midpoint is re-probed only when the upper half comes back empty, which is what makes far-ahead never worse than the midpoint.

claims.statement: Swath's internal key ranges are disjoint and cover the keyspace with no gap or overlap.
claims.qualification: Five source-established mechanisms close distinct hazards: exact seed tiling ending in a final open range, a single strict k greater-than hi so a boundary key belongs left, a per-key bound re-read backed by an under-lock re-trim whose downstream emission uses the trimmed batch, a three-clause durable compare-and-swap, and two loser paths of which only the late one restores the bound. This is a source-established design property; no run instruments the internal ranges, and the zero-duplicate observation run is consistent with it but does not verify it.

claims.statement: Every range split is committed by a three-clause compare-and-swap whose UPDATE and child INSERT run in one checkpoint-writer transaction, so a crash mid-split leaves both rows or neither.
claims.qualification: A rowcount of zero aborts the split and the child is not inserted. The cursor-less-than-pivot clause is also the durable backstop that makes a badly placed pivot a balance bug rather than a coverage bug. Durability applies only where the checkpoint is on disk.

claims.statement: Swath's disjoint half-open key ranges are designed to produce exactly-once output by construction, needing no separate deduplication pass.
claims.qualification: This is the documented and source-established range model. Seed pages never emit objects, so seed-to-range double emission is structurally impossible. Crash-path exactly-once remains unsettled and is covered by claim exactly-once-under-crash.

claims.statement: The default shallow seed runs a serial delimiter-slash descent whose probe budget is derived from the worker count, so raising --concurrency lengthens the seed phase.
claims.qualification: targetSeeds is min(1000, four times workers) and maxProbes is min(256, targetSeeds); the frontier is polled one node at a time. The lengthening is upstream's own stated consequence and is corroborated by the serial loop structure, not measured here.

claims.statement: Pagination is purely start_after set to the last emitted key; ContinuationToken is never sent and the response's NextContinuationToken is carried but unused.
claims.qualification: Upstream's stated reason is that range stealing needs an arbitrary sub-range lower bound, which an opaque token cannot express; most of the rest of the engine design follows from this one decision.

claims.statement: The --concurrency flag is an AIMD ceiling rather than a setpoint: a run starts at min(4, N) permits and the store, not the flag, sets the steady-state level; since 0.3.0 upstream's own help text and docs say so.
claims.qualification: This is the most consequential tunable fact for a benchmark. tMax appears only as an upper clamp: growth is min(tMax, T times 2) while slow-starting and min(tMax, T plus 1) afterwards, and every decrease is max(1, floor(factor times T)). At v0.2.0 the CLI help called the flag 'Maximum concurrent listing requests', so the ceiling reading had to be established from source; at 0.3.1 the help reads 'AIMD ceiling for concurrent listing requests (default: 64)' and docs/configuration.md and algorithms.md section 5 document it, adding that the controller never lowers T for efficiency, so a clean endpoint can run at the full ceiling. A benchmark reading --concurrency N as N concurrent requests will still be wrong; effective concurrency must be instrumented separately.

claims.statement: Swath's AIMD controller adapts live concurrency to 503 throttling, multiplicatively decreasing the permit gauge on a 503 or SlowDown and additively re-increasing it across clean windows.
claims.qualification: The throttle decrease factor is 0.7 and counts as a real AIMD vote; a separate sustained-timeout shed uses factor 0.5 once per jittered 25 to 40 second window. Growth is additionally gated by a hard worker-timeout freeze and a latency-inflation freeze. Whether the controller was ever exercised is a separate, unanswered question: the one retained run summary records zero throttle events (claim aimd-necessity).

claims.statement: Swath's AIMD 503 controller may be dead weight if listing is latency-bound rather than throttle-bound.
claims.qualification: This is an open hypothesis, not a finding. It is a scale and concurrency question that a single prefix-scale run against a clean public bucket cannot reach.

evidence.reason: No throttling or high-concurrency scenario has exercised the controller; the one retained run summary records zero errors against a clean public bucket.

claims.statement: SDK-internal retry is disabled at maxAttempts 1, so one increment of Swath's API counter corresponds to one SDK list-call attempt and the AIMD gauge sees every real 503 immediately.
claims.qualification: The value is hard-wired and not CLI-tunable. This is what makes cost.api_calls a meaningful request count rather than a call-site count.

claims.statement: Because the liveness watchdog is armed by default, the production retry policy is RIDE_OUT: over-cap transient faults retry indefinitely at a 15 second backoff ceiling and the watchdog owns termination.
claims.qualification: The two retry loops differ: on the engine path an AIMD-voting throttle resets the transient counter, so a permanently throttling endpoint can never trip the eight-retry cap, while on the seed path every throttle counts toward it and is never reset. Since 0.3.0 the seed path has one non-retried case: a probe failure whose cause chain contains a connection refusal or unknown host is fatal at once (ListingException, reason seed_endpoint_unreachable) instead of entering the ride-out; this applies only to the seed decorator built by TransientRetryFetcher.forSeed, not to the engine fetcher or mid-run structure probes. Disarming both watchdog tripwires selects BOUNDED, which cancels the run as resumable exit 75.

claims.statement: The liveness watchdog carries two independent tripwires with separate clocks: a 120 second total-freeze window fed by any progress signal including retry activity, and a 10 minute zero-real-progress window fed only by committed work.
claims.qualification: The operational consequence read from source is that a sustained-throttling run keeps re-arming the 120 second wire and ends at the 10 minute wire instead; that outcome is untested here, since neither run saw a single throttle event. The escalation ladder is cooperative cancel, then forensic dump plus interrupt after 10 seconds, then Runtime.halt(75) after a further 60 seconds.

claims.statement: The --request-rate limiter is a zero-burst capacity-one bucket that wraps the page fetcher inside the retry loops, so every retry attempt also pays the rate-limit wait.
claims.qualification: Refill is one token every round(1e9 divided by rps) nanoseconds, deliberately fixed-interval and stated as part of the public contract. The interaction with retries is read from the wrapping order and has not been exercised.

claims.statement: The observed parallelism ratio holds at concurrency above eight and at larger scopes.
claims.qualification: Nothing above one prefix-scale run at the default ceiling has been measured. The behaviour on larger buckets is unmeasured, and the ceiling-not-setpoint finding means the sweep must instrument effective concurrency rather than the flag.

evidence.reason: No concurrency sweep has been run and concurrency behaviour is scale-dependent. One unreplicated v0.3.1 round-trip on 2026-09-02 ran the prefix at the adapter's default ceiling of 64 and self-reported peak 18 in flight with average 6.98 (../receipts/observations-v0.3.1/adapter-modes/stderr.recursive-tsv.txt); a single prefix-scale run at one setting is not a ratio measurement.

claims.statement: Swath sets encoding-type=url on every request and, since 0.3.0, percent-decodes the response keys itself: a swath-owned execution interceptor streams the ListObjectsV2 XML, applies the SDK's URLDecoder-backed SdkHttpUtils.urlDecode to each Key and CommonPrefixes/Prefix, and hands the SDK an empty body, so the SDK's own DecodeUrlEncodedResponseInterceptor no longer sees the keys on the production path.
claims.qualification: Inbound, the decoded string is converted straight to bytes with a plain UTF-8 encode; outbound, a bound is rendered byte-exactly provided it is valid UTF-8, which holds by construction because synthesized pivots are built over Unicode code points. The decode semantics are the same java.net.URLDecoder call the SDK used, so the byte-exact round trip for non-ASCII keys, literal percent sequences and control bytes is preserved; the pre-0.3.0 SDK-model path survives only as a fallback that fires when the interceptor did not populate the page (metered as S3_RESPONSE/direct_page_absent), which is the path the older FakeS3Client unit tests still exercise.

claims.statement: A literal plus sign in a key survives byte-exactly only if the endpoint percent-encodes it, because swath's streaming response interceptor decodes keys with the SDK's SdkHttpUtils.urlDecode, which is java.net.URLDecoder and maps plus to space.
claims.qualification: This is conditional rather than observed. The tested LocalStack build does percent-encode plus and an in-tree integration test asserts the round trip through the production fetcher, whose client is built by S3ClientFactory and therefore carries swath's interceptor; a unit test also shows %2B decoding to a literal plus. That real AWS S3 also percent-encodes plus is assumed and is established by no in-tree test, since nothing in the repository runs against real S3. Against an endpoint that echoes plus literally under encoding-type=url, every such key would be silently corrupted to a space with no error. No such endpoint was seen here.

claims.statement: Swath has no validation that an endpoint honoured encoding-type=url: its own streaming interceptor decodes keys only when the response's echoed EncodingType is a case-sensitive exact match for 'url', and otherwise emits the wire form as if it were the key.
claims.qualification: An endpoint that percent-encodes but omits or misspells the echo fails the gate, skips the decode, and Swath emits the percent-encoded form as if it were the key, with no error. At v0.2.0 the gate lived in the pinned SDK jar and was established by disassembly; since 0.3.0 it is visible in Swath's main source tree (the response-side EncodingType reference in StreamingListObjectsV2Interceptor), mirroring the SDK's semantics. Upstream's compatibility note still describes the SDK decode as unconditional and does not mention the gate.

claims.statement: Four protocol-violation defences refuse a malformed page loudly: an oversized page and an unparseable or wrongly-rooted success body in the store, and a truncated-but-empty page and a stuck cursor with no forward progress in the engine.
claims.qualification: Both engine guards run before the consumer callback, so a broken page is never committed or emitted; since 0.3.0 the forward-progress guard also covers the terminal (non-truncated) page, so a last page that repeats or regresses the cursor is fatal where v0.2.0 accepted it. The oversized-page violation is a fatal non-retried ProtocolViolationException at exit 1 that outranks every cancellation code in exit-code resolution; the streamed-XML failure is an SdkClientException that the fault classifier treats as fatal unless an IOException sits in its cause chain, in which case it is retried as a network fault. An <Error> document under HTTP 200 is routed to the SDK's normal error handling rather than parsed as a page. The defences cover quantity, parseability, pagination liveness and synthesis safety only; intra-page ordering and the encoding contract are uncovered.

claims.statement: Swath assumes each page arrives in ascending unsigned byte order and never checks it: a page whose interior keys are unordered passes unexamined so long as its last key advances the cursor.
claims.qualification: The absence was established by an exhaustive read of the scan loop and a repository-wide search of the core and S3 main source trees; the forward-progress guard compares only the last key against the previous cursor. Only a replay server can exercise the failure, so it is a source-established gap, not an observed one.

claims.statement: A key inserted behind a cursor the scan has already passed is missed, as with any paginated lister.
claims.qualification: Upstream documents the behaviour and the companion structural-zero-overlap half is corroborated by the disjointness mechanisms, but insertion behaviour under concurrent mutation is not something source can settle and no mutating-bucket or replay experiment was run.

evidence.reason: No concurrent-mutation or replay experiment was run; source cannot settle behaviour against a bucket that changes mid-listing.

claims.statement: Swath produces exactly-once output across a crash and resume.
claims.qualification: No crash, SIGKILL, or resume run was performed at v0.2.0. Both runs wrote to stdout, which resolves --checkpoint auto to an in-process memory-backed store that is never resumable, so the crash path could not have been exercised even incidentally.

evidence.reason: No crash, SIGKILL, or resume run was performed; resume under crash is a scale-and-fault scenario neither observation run could reach.

claims.statement: Swath's text output formats are lossy for keys outside plain UTF-8 printable bytes: the streaming and dataset-part TSV writers and the table writer escape control bytes as backslash-xHH without escaping the backslash itself, and every text format renders a key that is not well-formed UTF-8 through a decode that turns invalid bytes into U+FFFD irreversibly.
claims.qualification: At v0.3.1 the escaper is unchanged and still not bypassable (--raw-output has no option binding; new runs always escape). Partitioned TSV parts use a byte-oriented formatter that copies well-formed UTF-8 key bytes verbatim and applies the same backslash-xHH escape, so a key literally containing backslash-x-0-9 remains indistinguishable from a key containing a tab on every TSV and table sink; an adapter must detect and refuse, never decode. The U+FFFD loss is reachable only from replay fixtures or captures that carry non-UTF-8 key bytes: both live S3 paths build key bytes by UTF-8-encoding the SDK's decoded key string, so a live listing cannot produce such a key. The last_modified field of the streaming TSV row now also passes through the control escaper.

claims.statement: JSONL is the only invertible text format, because its JSON escaping also escapes the backslash itself.
claims.qualification: JSONL emits no header and omits nullable fields rather than emitting nulls, so an adapter must key on field names and never on position. Invertibility is a property of the escaping only; a key containing bytes that are not valid UTF-8 is still lost to U+FFFD before the formatter sees it.

claims.statement: The TSV format always writes a header line and emits six fields with last_modified before etag.
claims.qualification: This is the one place a normalizer needs separation logic on an otherwise clean stdout stream: the header must be dropped and columns three and four swapped to reach the study's field order. At v0.3.1 the same six-column header also opens every partitioned TSV part (plain, .gz or .zst), so a dataset reader must drop one header per part, and the manifest's fileSchema names the same columns. Only ObjectEntry rows are emitted, so every row is six fully populated fields with row_type OBJECT; the last_modified column now carries the endpoint's own timestamp text (see timestamp-precision-is-variable), passed through the control escaper.

claims.statement: The Parquet key column stores the key's raw bytes in physical BINARY with no string decode, so it is byte-exact for every key it accepts; at v0.3.1 it is annotated STRING and the writer rejects a key that is not well-formed UTF-8 with a typed output error, so Parquet is no longer a path that can carry a non-UTF-8 key at all.
claims.qualification: Follows from source only. Because the column is now STRING, DuckDB reads it as VARCHAR (str) rather than BLOB (bytes): the study normalizer's comment that the key 'is Parquet BLOB' and reaches the emit boundary as raw bytes is stale, and byte-exactness must be checked as UTF-8 bytes of the returned string. For the keys Parquet accepts (all well-formed UTF-8, which is every key a live listing can produce) the text sinks' UTF-8 decode is lossless too, so Parquet's remaining advantage over TSV/table is only the absence of the ambiguous backslash-xHH escape; JSONL shares that advantage. Non-UTF-8 keys can now be lost nowhere and published nowhere: text sinks replace them with U+FFFD, Parquet fails the run.

claims.statement: The aligned format writes size and time at fixed widths of fourteen and twenty-four and the study's adapter reads fixed column offsets; the time field is now the endpoint's own LastModified text, so any spelling longer than twenty-four characters shifts the key column.
claims.qualification: At v0.3.1 S3's wire form YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.000Z is exactly twenty-four characters, so it fills the time column with no padding and the offsets 1-14 / 17-40 / 43-end still hold, as the study's retained 0.3.1 table sample shows for the rows it holds; the padding helper appends without padding when the gap is not positive, so an adapter must keep asserting the two separator spaces and refuse otherwise. A six-digit fraction (twenty-seven characters, possible on the epoch-micros fallback path) or any longer wire spelling would overflow. The formatter still emits neither etag nor storage class.

claims.statement: Swath's text sinks write last_modified as text whose spelling is the endpoint's: on the production S3 path the LastModified element text is passed through verbatim, and an entry rebuilt from epoch micros (compatibility SDK path, sort staging, fixtures) is rendered with zero, three or six fractional digits depending on the value; a zero or absent timestamp renders as an empty string.
claims.qualification: The v0.2.0 ISO_INSTANT rendering (Fields.isoMicros) no longer exists. Because S3 spells LastModified with millisecond precision, a live 0.3.1 run against S3 emits YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.000Z (source proves the pass-through; the study's retained 0.3.1 JSONL and table samples show that spelling on every retained row, and the round-trip's fraction stripping fired on all 2,549 rows of each text mode), so a normalizer's unconditional fraction stripping is now exercised on every row rather than being a hedge; any other endpoint spelling the AWS SDK grammar accepts (for example a +0000 offset) would reach the text sinks unchanged, and the Parquet sink parses it lazily. The empty-string sentinel still collides with a real 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z on the rendering path.

claims.statement: Swath's native output faithfully preserves keys containing control characters.
claims.qualification: Not exercised at v0.2.0: the study registry configures no edge-case bucket, and the corpus listed carries no such keys. Settling it needs a seeded edge corpus plus a capture path that does not pass through the lossy text escaping.

evidence.reason: No control-character key corpus was configured or run; the registry records EDGE_BUCKET as none.

claims.statement: During a listing run the only writer of file descriptor 1 in Swath's main source tree is the output sink; logging, progress, the stats block and the resolved-output echo all go to stderr. The single other stdout writer is the --tune help / --tune KEY=? path, which prints and exits before any listing starts.
claims.qualification: Established by an exhaustive grep of the main source tree at v0.3.1 (swath-cli, swath-core, swath-model, swath-s3): FileDescriptor.out in OutputOptions.openSink and System.out in ListCommand.call are the only hits. A normalizer therefore still needs no stream-separation logic on a listing run, the one caveat being the TSV header line; it must, however, know that --compression gzip|zstd (or a .gz/.zst -o name) makes the stdout bytes a compressed stream, and that --format discard writes no rows to stdout at all.

claims.statement: Output is streaming rather than accumulate-then-dump: the output stage receives one page batch at a time and writes each entry straight through the formatter, holding no per-run collection.
claims.qualification: Each formatter reuses a single small string builder and the only per-run state is a four-counter tally. The split tree and cursors live in SQLite rather than on the heap. Parquet part metadata and sort staging metadata are explicitly outside this invariant.

claims.statement: The --object-listing-queue-size knob is an in-flight entry budget rather than a slot count, and admission tests the budget before adding a whole batch, so in-flight entries can transiently exceed it by one S3 page.
claims.qualification: End and failure items weigh zero, and a single batch larger than the capacity is still admitted on an empty channel so the pipeline cannot deadlock; the backing queue is unbounded and the weight gate is the only bound.

claims.statement: Swath's memory stays bounded by configuration rather than bucket size at large scale.
claims.qualification: The streaming output stage and the bounded entry queue say memory should be flat in object count for the text modes, but memory cliffs and OOM behaviour are scale-dependent and no cliff was probed. The round-trip's TSV run self-reported 287 MB peak RSS on a 2,549-key prefix, JVM-baseline-dominated and not a scale result. At v0.3.1 the growth paths to target are the bounded dataset writer pool, whose queue is capped process-wide and whose writers above four are admitted against heap, and the sorted finalization pipeline, whose readers and encoders are admitted against heap and file-descriptor budgets; the v0.2.0 Parquet part-metadata re-serialization path no longer exists, manifests being written once at completion.

evidence.reason: Memory behaviour at scale is scale-dependent; a 2,549-key prefix cannot test it and no scale campaign has run.

claims.statement: The reported cost.api_calls figure has exactly one increment site, fires immediately before the SDK list call, and counts attempts issued across every request class.
claims.qualification: It counts timeouts, 503s and connection failures, not just successes, and covers worker pages, seed probes, thief pivot probes and delimiter structure probes. A repository-wide scan of the S3 module found no other request kind, so nothing is hidden. The value to quote is the summed meter reported as cost.api_calls or the api_calls field of the list_run_summary stderr line, not a single meter row and not the unwired private accessor.

claims.statement: Swath v0.3.1 offers at least thirteen modes: three text formats to a stream or single file, two partitioned text directory datasets (TSV and JSONL), a diagnostic discard sink, Parquet as a single-file sink and as a directory dataset, sorted Parquet, the resume subcommand, and three seed modes; text outputs additionally carry a none/gzip/zstd compression axis.
claims.qualification: A mode is taken to be anything that changes the request pattern or the output contract. Everything added since v0.2.0 (discard, partitioned text datasets, compression) changes only the output contract; the listing engine and checkpoint path are shared, and the discard sink is explicitly built to measure the listing engine with the material output path removed. The seed-mode axis remains the only supported control over whether Swath issues delimiter-slash requests at all; it is not a shallow output mode. The hints seed mode is still declared but unreachable.

claims.statement: Swath has no hinted seed mode: the hints seed mode is accepted by CLI validation and then throws an invalid-config error at seed time.
claims.qualification: The surface at v0.2.0 is --tune seed.mode=hints, and the failure is exit 2 raised after the checkpoint database is opened and the S3 client is built, so it is not a pure validation refusal. Swath still requires no up-front hints, unlike the two-pass hinted path of some other tools.

claims.statement: Swath v0.2.0 has no inspect or diff subcommand; the command surface is list, resume and help, plus two hidden commands, dump-run and completion.
claims.qualification: No inspect or diff classes exist at cef8ec2 and neither name appears in the command surface. A bare invocation with an S3 URI and no verb exits 2 with a did-you-mean hint pointing at swath list.

claims.statement: Swath has no delimiter or CommonPrefix output mode; swath list always fully enumerates objects and uses delimiter-slash only internally for seed and thief probes.
claims.qualification: There is no --delimiter and no --recursive flag; the only such option in the repository belongs to an internal replay-server benchmark command, and the list path hard-wires the OBJECTS listing mode. Their absence from the live help output was also observed directly, without a receipt. A caller wanting a shallow one-level listing has no such mode.

claims.statement: Page size is a hard-coded 1000 with no --max-keys flag, so it is not sweepable without patching source.
claims.qualification: The value is a local variable threaded into the range specs with no option feeding it; the only --max-keys in the repository belongs to an internal replay-server benchmark command. Its absence from the live help output was also observed directly, without a receipt. A cross-tool page-size axis must state this asymmetry rather than absorb it.

claims.statement: There is no --no-owner-split flag; the owner-split kill switch is spelled --engine-toggle owner_split=off, and since 0.3.0 --engine-toggle itself is a hidden diagnostic option that no longer appears in the installed help but still parses.
claims.qualification: The field exists with no option binding and a dedicated test asserts the flag spelling is rejected as an unmatched argument, while live javadoc and an unreachable error string still name it. --engine-toggle is documented under docs/configuration.md's diagnostic section rather than in swath list --help, and a golden test pins it hidden; docs/cli.md states that hidden options still parse.

claims.statement: Versioned listing is dead code: no --all-versions flag exists, nothing can set the VERSIONS listing mode, and the page fetcher throws for it.
claims.qualification: The enum value exists in the model and the checkpoint schema admits it, but the sole run-key construction passes the OBJECTS literal, so the branch is reachable only from a hand-crafted checkpoint database. Upstream documentation agrees that versioned listing is not implemented, while several other documents and javadoc still name the flag. Its absence from the live help output was also observed directly, without a receipt.

claims.statement: The fourteen --engine-toggle values are declared by the project to be experimental diagnostic surface rather than supported configuration, with one documented exception, and from 0.3.0 the flag is hidden from --help while still parsing.
claims.qualification: Several toggles change the request pattern outright, so by a request-pattern definition they would be modes; the resolution adopted here is that only the documented pre-0.2.0 rollback pair, rate_anchored_sensing=off with tail_floor=current, is a legitimate non-default engine configuration. An unknown name, bad value or contradictory repeat exits 2 before any I/O. At 0.3.1 the flag is hidden from help and shell completion (docs/cli.md) and its reference moved from docs/usage.md to the 'Diagnostic engine toggles' section of docs/configuration.md; the toggle set, defaults and parser are unchanged.

claims.statement: The v0.1.0 to v0.2.0 engine delta is two default flips: rate-anchored sensing off to on, and the tail floor from CURRENT to REACH_FLOORED.
claims.qualification: Both defaults are confirmed in the toggle record and its parse fallbacks, not only in prose. The old tail-floor reading was structurally blind rather than merely noisy, since its product is exactly zero for any estimate once the reach term is non-positive; the new one floors reach at one sixteenth. Each consult site also evaluates the old verdict and records the divergence, so the tool ships instrumentation for its own default flip.

claims.statement: Swath's filters are applied after listing and do not reduce API calls.
claims.qualification: Filters run in the fetch worker after the checkpoint commit and the in-range clamp, and nothing in the filter path touches the request. Two consequences: the include and exclude patterns are unanchored substring matches over a lossy string decode, and a verification run must use no filters at all, because a filtered run cannot be checked against a full-scope manifest.

claims.statement: The current Swath driver modes that use native Parquet sinks are not published by the current minimal attempt artifact contract.
claims.qualification: This is a limitation of the current driver and minimal artifact publication path, not a tool limitation or a claim that file sinks are permanently uncapturable. Swath refuses Parquet on stdout; command.py directs the Parquet probes to /tmp/swout, while the current attempt engine publishes only result.json and the two captured raw streams and does not collect native output.

claims.statement: Swath v0.2.0's Parquet and sorted-Parquet output paths execute as documented.
claims.qualification: No Parquet or sorted-Parquet run was made at v0.2.0. The current driver directs these modes to /tmp/swout and the minimal attempt contract does not publish native output, so both paths remain unexercised here.

evidence.reason: No Parquet or sorted-Parquet run was executed at v0.2.0; the current driver uses a container-local native sink that the minimal attempt contract does not publish.

claims.statement: Swath's Parquet and sorted-Parquet output faithfully contains every listed key.
claims.qualification: On 2026-09-02 the v0.3.1 image wrote a direct and a sorted Parquet dataset over the 2,549-key normals-hourly/ prefix, both read back through the normalizer to the same key set as the six text modes (../receipts/observations-v0.3.1/). That is an observation of count and cross-mode agreement on ASCII keys, not a completeness verdict: no reference-manifest verifier ran, no edge-key corpus exists, and the datasets were produced outside the benchmark worker. Source establishes that the key column is raw bytes and UTF-8-only, covered by claim parquet-key-column-is-byte-exact.

evidence.reason: No verifier verdict exists for any Parquet dataset: the 2026-09-02 round-trip established only count and cross-mode agreement over one ASCII-keyed prefix, outside the benchmark worker, with no edge corpus.

claims.statement: Swath lists a public bucket anonymously: --no-sign-request selects the anonymous credentials provider at the top of a three-branch resolution chain.
claims.qualification: Precedence is --no-sign-request over --profile over the SDK default chain, with bearer-token command auth as a fourth orthogonal path that replaces SigV4 entirely. Every mode of the 2026-09-02 round-trip listed anonymously from a credential-starved container and exited 0 (claim round-trip-count-and-cross-mode-agreement); single unreplicated observations, not receipts.

claims.statement: A run with no resolvable region exits 2 before the first request even with --no-sign-request, because region resolution and credential resolution are independent code paths.
claims.qualification: This is the single most likely reason a first containerized run fails. The invocation must carry --region, or a region environment variable, or an endpoint override that short-circuits to us-east-1. Since the 0.3.0 documentation rewrite upstream's anonymous quickstarts and operating guide carry --region us-east-1 explicitly and the FAQ documents the exit-2 failure; at v0.2.0 the quickstarts omitted it.

claims.statement: A wrong region is fatal rather than self-correcting: a 301 permanent redirect becomes a typed fatal error at exit 1 that is deliberately never retried.
claims.qualification: Upstream's stated reason is that the fetcher's client is long-lived and shared across every worker and thief thread. The error message carries the bucket's actual region header.

claims.statement: Swath maps failures onto eight exit codes: 0 for success, an empty result, an already-complete resume or a broken pipe; 1 unrecoverable; 2 bad arguments or a guarded refusal; 74 output filesystem full (EX_IOERR); 75 cooperative stuck and resumable; 124 timebox elapsed; and 130 or 143 for signals.
claims.qualification: The exception hierarchy is sealed, so the error-to-exit mapping is compiler-checked for exhaustiveness, and a protocol violation is searched for first through the cause chain and suppressed exceptions so it outranks every cancellation code, which all claim a resumable partial. Exit 74 (added in 0.2.2) is not a new exception type: OutputException derives it by searching its own cause chain for an out-of-space IOException, so the sealed permits list is unchanged. Upstream's usage and FAQ tables agree with source on all eight codes and add that 74, 75, 124, 130 and 143 imply resumable state only when the run uses a managed Parquet directory.

claims.statement: Swath's resume design uses a SQLite checkpoint whose listing_node table is the worklist, written by a single checkpoint-writer thread.
claims.qualification: At v0.3.1 the schema is still pinned at user_version 1 with exact-match-or-refuse and no version migration path, carrying run_meta, listing_node and part_file tables; additive nullable columns (run_meta context columns and, since 0.3.0, part_file.format_version and extension_type) are backfilled by the same idempotent ALTER TABLE step for fresh and older databases alike. The durable cursor is the highest key inside a finalized part, intended to give exactly-once for Parquet parts, a runtime property that claim exactly-once-under-crash leaves unverified; the plain cursor column still exists but no text sink is resumable any more, so its at-most-once semantic no longer reaches a user. The checkpoint is deleted on clean completion, so resuming a completed directory reports already complete and exits 0.

claims.statement: Swath resumes a crashed or interrupted listing from its SQLite checkpoint.
claims.qualification: This is a design read only. No crash, SIGKILL or mid-checkpoint resume run was performed at v0.2.0, and neither run could have exercised it: a stdout run gets an in-process memory-backed checkpoint, and the durable path needs a directory dataset the harness cannot mount.

evidence.reason: No SIGKILL or resume run was performed; resume under crash needs a durable checkpoint the observation runs never created.

claims.statement: Only a managed Parquet directory dataset is resumable: a stdout run, a --format discard run, or --checkpoint none opens an in-process memory-backed SQLite store that writes nothing to disk; a single-file destination and a partitioned TSV/JSONL directory dataset are both refused unless --checkpoint none is passed explicitly.
claims.qualification: Ephemeral is not the absence of SQLite: it is the same store and the same compare-and-swap machinery over an in-memory database, so committed is not always durable. The output directory, not a checkpoint path, is the run handle, and an arbitrary SQLite path is refused by swath resume. Since 0.3.0 a text directory dataset looks like a run handle on disk but carries no durable output journal, so both fresh creation (without --checkpoint none) and any later resume against it are refused with exit 2.

claims.statement: Every resumable option carries a first-class resume classification of identity, sticky or free, and a resume that changes an identity option is refused by name.
claims.qualification: The annotation sits on the same program element as the option so it can never name a wrong option, and a drift test covers every visible option. Identity covers the endpoint, format, output target and type, fetch-owner, sort, all seven filters, the seed mode and the argument-hash fields; sticky covers the four credential-shaped flags; both bearer-token flags are deliberately free and never persisted.

claims.statement: The resume subcommand exposes only the directory, bearer-token options, colour, progress, stats, tune and verbosity flags, so concurrency, queue size, request rate, the Parquet rotation knobs and the new text-dataset and writeback knobs cannot be varied across a resume boundary.
claims.qualification: It is the practical counterweight to the free resume classification, which means only that an option is not identity-bearing and will not be refused, not that it can be set on the resume command line. Of the tune keys, three are resume-applicable at 0.3.1: sort.merge-parallelism (the sorted merge's encoder count, safe to change because partial finals are disposable), sort.keep-staging and sort.ignore-disk-check. Evidence is the golden help capture, which is asserted byte-equal by test.

claims.statement: Transient S3 error classes are individually classified and retried, and only exact status-and-code pairs get a typed fatal subtype while any other 4xx falls through to the generic fatal listing exception.
claims.qualification: Not every 403 or 404 is specifically typed. At v0.2.0 the classifier deliberately logs under the page fetcher's logger name so the operational filter surface stays stable, and the exception hierarchy is sealed so the mapping is exhaustive by compilation.

claims.statement: Swath builds and runs on amd64.
claims.qualification: At v0.3.1 the published OCI index carries a real linux/amd64 child manifest, the continuous-integration workflow builds both platforms with no emulation action anywhere in the repository, and the release pipeline runs its container smoke on an amd64 runner. The study's own 2026-09-02 eight-mode adapter round-trip ran the amd64 child natively and exited 0 in every mode.

claims.statement: Upstream validates arm64 to build but never runtime-smokes it, because its runners are amd64.
claims.qualification: Still true at v0.3.1: the publish workflow says so outright and the release smoke runs its container on an amd64 runner. Risk is low, since the jar is arch-neutral, but non-zero for the native extraction paths. This study holds no arm64 runtime observation of v0.3.1; the round-trip ran the amd64 child.

claims.statement: At v0.3.1, as at v0.2.0, Swath's in-source javadoc and older prose are not a reliable statement of the shipped surface or the shipped defaults, while its reference tables, golden help captures, the new coverage-tested supported-surface page and the code are.
claims.qualification: Of the drift items re-checked at 0.3.1, the three engine-default javadoc items (D10, D11, D12) and both live error strings (D4, D15) persist verbatim, as do the --no-owner-split javadoc and unreachable conflict string (D5) and the --single-file reference (D7); the --all-versions name (D1) was removed from usage.md prose but survives in ROADMAP.md, contracts.md and javadoc; the s3-implementation-compatibility passage (D13) was reworded rather than retracted. On the other side, the 0.3.0 documentation rewrite added docs/cli.md, whose completeness against the visible option set is enforced by HelpUsageGoldenTest, and the flag/default tables in docs/configuration.md matched --tune help on every key checked. Items D2, D3, D6, D8, D9 and D14 were not re-audited here.

claims.statement: At the 2026-09-02 update date the Swath repository was 39 days old, created 2026-07-25, with one human contributor (134 contributions) plus dependabot; at the 2026-08-02 research date it was eight days old with 48 commits.
claims.qualification: Read from the GitHub repository and contributors APIs on 2026-09-02. A project-age and staffing fact that moves with time, not a judgement about the code; the sole contributor is also the sole reviewer of the protected public-release environment, which makes releases a single point of failure.

claims.statement: Upstream's scheduled Nightly deep verification workflow was intermittent at the 2026-09-02 reading, with five failures and three successes in the eight most recent runs, while pull-request and main continuous integration were green.
claims.qualification: On 2026-09-02 the runs of 08-27, 08-28 and 08-31 succeeded and those of 08-29, 08-30, 08-31, 09-01 and 09-02 failed, including the run at b6181a1, three commits before the v0.3.1 tag. The cause was not investigated and what that suite covers was not established, so this bounds the project's visible verification health and nothing more.

claims.statement: Two live runtime error messages tell the user to pass flags that do not exist: the unimplemented seed mode names --seed and --hints, and the sort disk guard names --force-sort.
claims.qualification: This is the sharpest operational half of the drift set. The real surfaces are --tune seed.mode and --tune sort.ignore-disk-check. The disk-guard message is printed immediately before the guard halts the process, so it reaches a user at the worst possible moment.

claims.statement: JVM startup and garbage collection cost Swath measurable throughput at high list rates.
claims.qualification: Not tested at high list rates. The round-trip's TSV run reported a 1.5 second listing phase inside a 2.7 second session on a 2,549-key prefix, consistent with JVM startup plus a serial seed descent, but that is one unreplicated prefix-scale observation and not a high-rate result.

evidence.reason: No high-list-rate run has been performed; behaviour at high rates is scale-dependent.

claims.statement: On a flat-root corpus the up-front shallow seed makes fewer API calls than no seed.
claims.qualification: No cost comparison of the two seed arms exists at v0.2.0. The seed.mode=none arm has been executed once through the rewritten adapter on one prefix, but only its output was captured, so the two arms have never been compared for cost; the seed-mode comparison is the cleanest experiment Swath offers and is the priority for the re-run.

evidence.reason: The one seed.mode=none run at v0.2.0 captured output only: no list_run_summary counters were recorded for it, and the two instrumented runs both used the default shallow seed, so no cost comparison of the two arms exists for this subject.

claims.statement: From 0.3.0 a seed probe that fails with a connection refusal or unknown host is fatal immediately, recorded as steal_reason FATAL/seed_endpoint_unreachable, instead of consuming the transient retry budget or riding out under the watchdog.
claims.qualification: Only the seed decorator built by TransientRetryFetcher.forSeed carries the flag; it is used by seedFreshRun, which runs for a fresh run and for a resume whose checkpoint holds zero nodes. The detection walks the ThrottleException cause chain for java.net.ConnectException or UnknownHostException. The engine fetcher and mid-run delimiter structure probes keep the ordinary retry loops. Exit-code mapping of the resulting ListingException is outside this reader's scope (ListCommand's comment at 1000-1002 calls a genuine fatal seed error exit 1).

claims.statement: Upstream documents at 0.3.0 that the AIMD controller is reactive backpressure only: a 503 or timeout storm can lower T and latency inflation can hold growth, but nothing lowers T for efficiency, so a clean endpoint can climb to a high T that only the --concurrency ceiling bounds, and Tmax must be sized by the operator from repeated runs rather than inferred from a run that never hit it.
claims.qualification: Design prose in the algorithm reference plus a new 'Choosing --concurrency' section; the controller source that implements it is unchanged from 0.2.0. Upstream explicitly says a replay experiment on one bucket or latency regime is not a universal S3 cap, which bears on the replay-backed benchmark design.

claims.statement: The engine's no-forward-progress guard now also fires on a non-truncated terminal page whose last key does not advance past the previous cursor; at v0.2.0 the terminal page was exempt.
claims.qualification: An empty terminal page remains legitimate and leaves the cursor unchanged. The guard runs before the consumer callback, so the offending page is not emitted; the failure is a plain ListingException at exit 1. A replay server or S3-compatible endpoint that repeats the cursor key on its last page, which v0.2.0 tolerated, is now refused.

claims.statement: Every S3 request carries an HTTP User-Agent beginning with swath/<version> (swath/development outside a packaged build) ahead of the SDK's own aws-sdk-java and api/S3 markers, so swath traffic is attributable in S3 server access logs, CloudTrail and any endpoint that logs callers.
claims.qualification: Added in 0.2.4; no request behaviour changes. A benchmark author can filter server-side logs on the prefix and should expect the tool to be identifiable to the endpoint operator. The version is read from the jar manifest Implementation-Version.

claims.statement: Since 0.3.0 successful ListObjectsV2 bodies are parsed by a swath-owned StAX interceptor that builds the page model directly from the wire XML and hands the SDK an empty result, bypassing the SDK's XmlElement tree and response model on the production path.
claims.qualification: The SDK still owns marshalling, HTTP, auth, timeouts, retry decisions and error-body handling; only 2xx ListObjectsV2 bodies are intercepted. The parser is Woodstox 7.2.2, pinned explicitly on the swath-s3 runtime classpath. Engagement is metered: swath.steal_reason S3_RESPONSE/direct_page (production), streaming_xml (SDK-model callers), direct_page_absent (fallback to the old SDK-model conversion), sdk_error_in_success (an <Error> document under HTTP 200, re-serialized and routed to the SDK's error handler); FATAL/streaming_xml_unparseable marks a body the streamer could not parse, surfaced as SdkClientException 'Unable to stream ListObjectsV2 XML response'. Consequences for a benchmark author: key percent-decoding now happens in swath (same URLDecoder semantics, same case-sensitive EncodingType echo gate); last-modified text is preserved unparsed; and the per-call-class latency phases shift, since the SDK's sdk_unmarshal phase now contains swath's streaming parse while the fetcher's response_parse phase measures little more than list assignment.

claims.statement: At v0.3.1 the Parquet key column is BINARY annotated STRING, and the writer fails the run with a typed InvalidKeyEncodingException when a key is not well-formed UTF-8, so a swath Parquet dataset can only ever contain valid UTF-8 keys and DuckDB reads the column as VARCHAR.
claims.qualification: Physical bytes, statistics and ordering are unchanged from 0.2.x datasets and old datasets are not rewritten. A live listing cannot trigger the rejection because both S3 paths UTF-8-encode the SDK's decoded key string; it affects re-publishing or sorting a capture that holds non-UTF-8 keys. A normalizer that read the column as BLOB must now treat it as text and compare UTF-8 bytes.

claims.statement: Text sinks write last_modified as the endpoint's LastModified text on the production S3 path, so rows listed from S3 carry its spelling, YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.000Z in the study's retained 0.3.1 samples; only entries rebuilt from epoch micros are rendered by swath (0, 3 or 6 fraction digits, empty for zero).
claims.qualification: Replaces the v0.2.0 ISO_INSTANT rendering. Parquet still stores TIMESTAMP(MICROS,UTC) by parsing the text lazily (ObjectEntry.lastModifiedEpochMicros); a malformed text fails there with LastModifiedParseException rather than at the text sink. The aligned table's 24-character time column is exactly filled by S3's spelling.

claims.statement: --format discard (0.3.0) runs the normal work-stealing listing, checkpoint commit-before-emit, bounded channel and emission metrics but writes no rows, so it isolates listing cost from output cost; it refuses -o, refuses --compression, and is non-resumable.
claims.qualification: The stage tallies rows, object bytes and emitted-entry progress exactly as a material sink would, so api_calls and the run report remain comparable with other modes; only the formatter/writer path is absent. It still needs --checkpoint none only in the sense that it cannot carry a durable checkpoint (stdout-kind destination).

claims.statement: Since 0.3.0 a TSV or JSONL directory destination is a bounded multi-writer partitioned text dataset (--text-writers 2-64, default 3; --text-part-size default 256mb; optional gzip or zstd per part; manifest and _SUCCESS), sharing the Parquet writer-pool model; only --format table is refused for a directory.
claims.qualification: Parts are named with the format suffix plus .gz/.zst; the manifest format is the text format name. Writer count and part size are FREE resume options but the dataset itself is not resumable. --writeback-size (default off, minimum 4mb) shapes filesystem writeback for text and Parquet parts without changing rotation or crash recovery.

claims.statement: A partitioned TSV/JSONL dataset must be created with --checkpoint none: any other checkpoint mode is refused at argument validation, a resume whose checkpoint records a text directory is refused, and the text runner refuses a resumed run.
claims.qualification: The refusal text is 'partitioned text datasets are non-resumable in this release; pass --checkpoint none' (exit 2). The --checkpoint help and ResumeCommand javadoc were updated to say the same; upstream's 0.3.0 release notes list stdout, text files, text datasets, discard and the legacy .parquet one-writer layout as non-resumable.

claims.statement: --compression none|gzip|zstd (0.3.0) compresses table/TSV/JSONL streams, files and dataset parts; it is inferred from a .gz/.zst -o extension, conflicts with a mismatching extension, and is refused for Parquet and discard.
claims.qualification: Compression is applied per part for datasets and to the whole stream for stdout. It is a FREE resume option only nominally, since no compressed output is resumable.

claims.statement: A --sort resume whose checkpoint records staging segments in a different page-run format name, or with missing or unsupported format_version/extension_type metadata, is refused before any staging file is touched and told to --restart; a 0.2.x sorted run interrupted mid-listing cannot be resumed by 0.3.x.
claims.qualification: The check runs only for --sort resumes and reads part_file.format/format_version/extension_type, two nullable columns added by additive migration in 0.3.0. Published Parquet datasets are unaffected; only an in-progress _staging directory is.

claims.statement: --tune sort.merge-parallelism=1..16 (0.3.0) sets the maximum number of concurrent final-file encoders in the sorted merge; its default is core-derived, max(1, min(8, cores/2)), so --tune help prints a machine-dependent default (4 in the published image), and it is resume-applicable because partial finals are disposable.
claims.qualification: Runtime heap and file-descriptor gates may admit fewer encoders than requested, and encoder count does not determine output part count. It supersedes the removed swath.sort.merge-parallelism JVM property. sort.keep-staging=on (diagnostic) retains checkpoint-tracked staging after a successful sorted publish.

claims.statement: Sorted Parquet parts are named part-00000.parquet upward while the footer key swath.sort.file_index remains one-based, so part-00000.parquet carries file_index=1.
claims.qualification: A consumer deriving an index from the filename sees a one-position shift relative to 0.2.x. Part geometry no longer depends on encoder count and sorted part bytes differ from a 0.2.4 run over the same bucket (release notes v0.3.0); row content and order are unaffected.

claims.statement: Direct Parquet and text datasets write manifest.json exactly once, at successful close, immediately before .swath-state.json, symlink.txt and _SUCCESS; no incomplete consumer manifest is emitted during a run.
claims.qualification: The checkpoint (part_file + durable_cursor) rather than the manifest is the resume authority for Parquet. A normalizer that gated on manifest.json alone would see nothing for a killed run; gating on _SUCCESS is the intended contract.

claims.statement: --tune parquet.writers now accepts 2..64 (was 2..4); values above 4 are admitted only when the JVM maximum heap covers a conservative per-writer memory plan, otherwise the run is refused with the admissible maximum named.
claims.qualification: A single-file .parquet destination still collapses to one writer. The heap gate makes the effective ceiling machine-dependent, so a sweep must record the JVM heap alongside the writer count.

claims.statement: Since 0.3.0 docs/cli.md is the explicit supported CLI surface: it names every option visible in swath list --help and swath resume --help, a golden test requires every one of the 49 visible options to appear there, and the diagnostic --engine-toggle option and dump-run command are hidden from help but still parse.
claims.qualification: Hidden means hidden = true on the picocli option or command, pinned by HelpUsageGoldenTest; the option set itself did not shrink. --tune remains the single visible door to expert keys, each declared stable, experimental or diagnostic by --tune help.
